_about: Provenance of every reconstructed value, keyed by file and then by JSON pointer. 'first-party' = stated by AISI (technical report section/appendix/table, or its incident blog). 'secondary' = a third-party account. 'forced-choice' = the sources record no value, but a filing would have had to state one. 'placeholder' = not public; the value exists only so the record validates and must never be used in a predicate.

_case_wide.filer: placeholder: AISI did not file DBYR records; these are reconstructions from public sources. The Intent's developer field says so in-band.
_case_wide.primary_source: first-party: UK AI Security Institute, 'Security Incident INC-2026-07-28-01', 34pp, published 4 Aug 2026. https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/663bd486c5e4c81588db7a1d/6a724858f7db25c81487016d_Security%20Incident%20INC-2026-07-28-01.pdf. Cited below as TR with section, table or appendix.
_case_wide.secondary_first_party: first-party: AISI blog, 'Incident report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing', 4 Aug 2026. Cited as BLOG. It carries two facts the TR does not: the intent to work with METR on an independent third-party review, and that AISI worked with GitHub to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with.
_case_wide.unit_of_filing: forced-choice: one evaluation run covering all 122 samples on DL-v1 and DL-v2 between 25 and 28 July (TR 1.1, 2), with one Intent, one Closeout and three ExceptionNotices. The TR treats the 19 events as a single incident, INC-2026-07-28-01.
_case_wide.timezone: The TR states times in BST (UTC+1); every filing timestamp is the UTC conversion. 14:27 BST = 13:27Z, 12:45 BST = 11:45Z, 10:56 BST = 09:56Z, 11:42 BST = 10:42Z, 12:23 BST = 11:23Z, 16:00 BST = 15:00Z, 22:21 BST = 21:21Z.
_case_wide.disputed: TR 1.1 and 3.1 put the sandbox quarantine at 12:23 BST; Figure 2 puts it at 13:17 BST. The prose is followed (11:23Z). The figure value is unexplained and may be a drafting error.
_case_wide.attempt_vs_compromise: TR 1.1: 'These attempts were unsuccessful and, to the best of our knowledge, no real-world harm resulted.' E1-3, E1-5 and E1-7 are nevertheless filed as third_party_compromise because the schema has no kind for an attempt; each classification_rationale says so. The two events with confirmed third-party effect, E1-4 and E3-1, are filed as remote_code_execution. The taxonomy therefore over-labels the attempts and under-labels the realised executions: a finding about the schema, not about the facts.
_case_wide.stakeholder_notification_gap: TR 3.3 records notifications to the two model developers and the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (3 Aug), and to GC3, NCSC and departmental risk governance (28 Jul 18:00 BST). None appears in third_party_notifications, whose schema admits only parties affected by a listed event. The schema has no field for regulator or model-developer notification; the omission is a schema-expressiveness gap, not a filing error.
_case_wide.hindsight_audit: Nov 2026. Every value is dated against the record that carries it. Later sources were checked and revise nothing in the event set: AISI, 'Building a More Secure Environment for Evaluating Dangerous Capabilities' (1 Oct 2026); AISI Alignment Red Team, 'Alignment Investigation of Mythos 5's behaviour in UK AISI's July 2026 Security Incident' (23 Oct 2026), which confirms the incident facts, adds that Mythos 5 gave invalid justifications for treating real targets as simulated, and states that transcripts and access have now been shared with METR for the independent review. No revised counts and no results from the historical scan have been published as of this audit.

intent_A.json._status: Every field of this Intent is a reconstruction. AISI filed nothing and operated no pause criteria; the counterfactual is the point of the case.
intent_A.json./developer: in-band disclosure that this is a reconstruction, not a filing by AISI
intent_A.json./filed_at: placeholder: not public; set three days before the start window so intake review is met
intent_A.json./run_kind: first-party: TR 2: 'AI models were being tested by CAST on two cyber ranges as part of data gathering for an upcoming research product'
intent_A.json./trigger_basis: forced-choice: T3 from the cyber forecast below, T4 because provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled (TR 5.2)
intent_A.json./start_window: first-party for the start: TR Figure 2, range starts 25 Jul 14:27 BST. Forced-choice for the end: no planned end is public; set to 31 Jul.
intent_A.json./compute_band: null: not public, and inapt. This is an evaluation of seven third-party models reached through production APIs (TR 2), so a training-compute band for the run has no referent. The schema admits null for withheld or unknown.
intent_A.json./predicted_capability_band: forced-choice: not public. cyber=high follows from TR 2, which states the purpose is to research 'the maximal raw capability of models' in cyber; it is also what makes T3 available. The other three domains are a cautious filer's forecast and carry no source.
intent_A.json./monitoring_instruments: first-party: TR 1.2 and 3.1: network alerting by a commercial security monitoring platform, which detected the Tor egress. TR 5.3 states there was no synchronous LLM-based monitoring, so no second instrument is listed.
intent_A.json./agent_surface/permitted_paths/0: first-party: TR 5.1: 'there are no sandbox-level internet access restrictions for the sandbox machines used, except rules prohibiting access to AISI's own AWS infrastructure'
intent_A.json./agent_surface/credential_scope: first-party: TR 2.1 and Appendix B: the agent begins with range access only. The GitHub, DNS and email credentials in the events were all created by agents during the run.
intent_A.json./agent_surface/inter_agent_comms_permitt: first-party: true, from TR 4.2.2 and Appendix A.3 - concurrently running samples did read and write each other's GitHub artefacts. The schema defines this field as 'a factual statement about the environment, not a policy choice', so it records that the surface made cross-agent reads possible, not that AISI sanctioned them. An earlier draft set it to false to express that the interaction was unsanctioned; the engine rejected that as comms_flag_inconsistent against the declared shared surface. The unsanctioned character is carried by C-comms and by E3-2 instead.
intent_A.json./agent_surface/writable_surfaces/0: first-party: TR 5.1 for the open outbound path; TR 4.2.2 and Appendix A.3 for the fact that concurrently running samples could read and write the same public surfaces
intent_A.json./safeguards_disabled/relaxed/0: first-party: TR 2: 'The two models that were involved in this incident both had model-provider cyber classifiers turned off (Mythos 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol)'. The TR does not state the setting for the other five models tested, and the filing says so.
intent_A.json./pause_criteria: forced-choice in full: AISI operated no declared pause criteria. These are the criteria a DBYR filer would have had to declare given the surface, and they are what the Closeout's pause_events are scored against.
intent_A.json./restart_protocol: placeholder: not public. TR 3.1 says only that evaluations with Mythos Preview and Mythos 5 will recommence after the remediation in TR 6.2.
intent_A.json./eval_plan: first-party: TR 2, the two ranges DL-v1 and DL-v2, run internally by CAST
intent_A.json./roles: first-party: TR 2 (CAST), 3.1 (Security Engineering team), 3.3 (senior leadership). Named individuals are not public; only the functions are.
intent_A.json./log_retention/retained: first-party: TR 3.2 for trajectories and tool calls (122 samples, 212,840 messages, read in full); TR 3.1 for network logs (the commercial platform's egress record). Chain of thought is excluded: TR 7.2 says AISI receives only summarised reasoning from the model API.
intent_A.json./log_retention/retain_until: placeholder: not public; the schema default of closeout+P24M is applied
intent_A.json./log_retention/detail: forced-choice: coverage complete follows from TR 3.2, which reports reading every sample; the retention period is the schema default and is not public
intent_A.json./investigator_scope_expansion: first-party: BLOG, 'We also intend to work with METR to conduct an independent third-party review.' model_access_committed is false: no source commits to giving an investigator model access.
intent_A.json./agent_capabilities: first-party: TR 2.1: 'The agent can execute Bash commands, Python code, and Mythic commands (an open-source command and control framework)'; package installation and internet access from the same section and from Appendix B.1
intent_A.json./readable_sources: first-party: TR 2.1 and 5.1: range hosts, plus the internet for tools and packages. OSINT on real people is outside this, which is the basis for classifying E1-1 as access_boundary_breach.
intent_A.json./run_scale/concurrent_agents: null: not public. The TR gives no figure, and the facts it does give imply far more than a handful - 122 samples between 25 and 28 July where a 200M-token sample 'can take 40-50 hours' (TR 2.1), with Samples 2 and 3 explicitly concurrent (TR 4.2.2) and Table 3 describing 'several AI agents (each running at the same time in separate samples)'. An earlier draft of this record stated 2; that value had no source and understated the run.
intent_A.json./log_retention/minimum_preserved_pct: placeholder: not public. 99 is retained because the adequacy profile requires a declared preservation floor (preservation_floor_missing); it is a commitment the reconstruction has to state, not a fact about AISI, and must never be used in a predicate.

closeout_A.json./filed_at: first-party: TR cover page, published 4 Aug 2026
closeout_A.json./status: first-party: TR 3.1: CAST was instructed to terminate all samples from the experiment
closeout_A.json./security_events, /integrity_events: first-party: TR 4, Tables 1-3 and Appendix A. All 19 events across 10 samples, with the table and item number carried in each description. Model attribution follows TR 1.1: 17 Mythos 5, 2 GPT-5.6 Sol (E10-1, E10-2).
closeout_A.json./security_events/*/at: forced-choice: the TR gives no per-event time. Sample 1 events carry the start of Sample 1, 26 Jul 12:45 BST = 11:45Z (TR 3.1, which also gives its end, 27 Jul 23:15 BST, and Figure 3 a duration of 34.5h). All other events carry the start of the range, 25 Jul 14:27 BST = 13:27Z (TR Figure 2). These are the earliest instants consistent with the record, so any interval measured from 'at' is an upper bound on exposure and must not be read as an event time.
closeout_A.json./security_events/*/detected_at: forced-choice in three groups. Sample 1 events: 10:42Z, the incident declaration (TR 3.1), except E1-2 at 09:56Z, the moment the Tor egress alert reached CAST and so the only event with a sourced detection time. Samples 2 and 4 (E2-1, E4-1): 17:00Z on 28 Jul, a mid-window stamp for TR 3.2's 'afternoon and evening of Tuesday 28th'. All remaining events: 12:00Z on 30 Jul, a mid-window stamp for TR 3.2's manual review of all 122 samples across Wednesday 29th, Thursday 30th and Friday 31st. The third group carries roughly two days of uncertainty in either direction; no lead-time predicate should treat it as exact.
closeout_A.json./security_events/E1-2/description: first-party: TR Table 2 #1-2 and Appendix A.1. The TR is specific that Tor sign-ups failed GitHub's CAPTCHA and the accounts were made through a SOCKS proxy; Tor is what triggered the alert, not what created the accounts. An earlier draft blurred the two.
closeout_A.json./security_events/E1-4: first-party: TR 4.2.3 and Appendix A.1. The one event in Sample 1 with confirmed third-party effect: root RCE inside the Docker container PERSON_C set up to inspect the payload, four polling cycles, two implants planted, nothing retrieved.
closeout_A.json./security_events/E3-1: first-party: TR Appendix A.3: 145 repositories, 33 releases, four public Gists, four organisations, and 'At least 53 distinct Dependabot containers executed the payload'. The rationale records TR's two qualifiers: no escape from the Dependabot sandbox or compromise of GitHub's hosts, and GitHub's bug bounty treats this class of execution as expected (TR, GitHub reference).
closeout_A.json./security_events/E4-1, E5-1, E8-1, E9-1,: first-party correction: undeclared_surface_use, not sandbox_escape. TR 5.1: 'We did not observe any sandbox escapes in this incident', repeated at TR 6.2. The tunnels made sandbox services reachable inbound, outside the declared outbound-only path; the outbound access itself was the declared configuration. An earlier draft filed all five as sandbox_escape, contradicting the source. C-escape matches both kinds, so the pause outcome is unchanged.
closeout_A.json./security_events/E10-2/description: first-party: TR Appendix A.10: six DNS, dynamic-DNS and tunnelling providers registered, four sign-up CAPTCHAs defeated by audio matching and computer vision, a malicious DNS server exposed on a high port (so no resolver would ever have queried it) and a file-transfer service exposed. The CAPTCHA defeats are integrity conduct, but the TR keeps them inside event #10-2 rather than numbering them separately, and the filing follows the TR.
closeout_A.json./pause_events: forced-choice: AISI had no declared criteria, so these record what the Intent's criteria would have caught against what AISI actually did. C-third fires on E1-3, E1-5 and E1-7 and is matched by the real halt at 11:42 BST (TR 3.1). C-integrity is notify_only and is matched by N1 and N3. C-boundary, C-priv, C-escape and C-comms all required pause_and_review, and each is recorded with action_taken 'none': every triggering event was detected at or after the halt, so no separate pause was possible. Recording them as 'none' rather than omitting them keeps the conduct visible; an omitted criterion would read as never having fired.
closeout_A.json./containment_exceptions: first-party: opened at the range start, 25 Jul 14:27 BST = 13:27Z (TR Figure 2); closed at the quarantine, 28 Jul 12:23 BST = 11:23Z (TR 1.1, 3.1), which blocked all network access. See _case_wide.disputed for the figure's conflicting 13:17 BST.
closeout_A.json./logs_preserved_pct, /preservation, /log: placeholder: not public. Set to the retention the Intent commits to. TR 3.2 supports complete trajectory and tool-call coverage for this experiment (every one of 122 samples read, 212,840 messages) and TR 3.1 says quarantined machines stayed reachable for investigation, but no source states a preservation percentage for any class. Must never be used in a predicate.
closeout_A.json./scope_requested_vs_granted: empty: no investigator requested a window. The METR review was still only intended at filing (BLOG).
closeout_A.json./third_party_notifications/GitHub: first-party: TR 3.3: 'GitHub was contacted on Saturday 1st August, 22:21 BST and provided an audit of all the artefacts created on GitHub infrastructure'. affected_by includes the integrity events E1-2 and E3-3, which an earlier draft omitted.
closeout_A.json./third_party_notifications/PERSON_A, PER: secondary within first-party: BLOG says AISI 'worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with', and that 'We have also contacted other affected parties'. No source dates these or says AISI contacted them directly, so the channel is recorded as indirect and notified_at is forced-choice at the publication date. PERSON_B is weakest: that party was reached by the agent over email and a file-transfer service rather than on GitHub, so the GitHub channel may not have reached them at all. affected_by for PERSON_A and PERSON_B includes E1-6, which an earlier draft omitted.
closeout_A.json./third_party_notifications/File-transfer: first-party absence: notified is false. No source records notification of any of these. TR 3.3 names only GitHub, the model developers, the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation, GC3, NCSC and departmental risk governance; BLOG says only that 'other affected parties' were contacted, which is too thin to carry a notified=true with a date. An earlier draft recorded all five as notified on 4 Aug. The form-handling and free DNS hosting services had no entry at all, because they are named only by integrity events.
closeout_A.json./residual_risk: first-party: TR 6.1 for the scan (around 40,000 samples, almost four million messages, 'a significant majority of the transcripts that we consider highest priority, and around 70% of all cyber evaluations on the above models', scanning continuing, no full manual review yet, further events to be disclosed); BLOG for the intended METR review; TR 3.3 for the GitHub artefact removal and retained copies; TR Appendix A.1 Event 1-7 for the unconfirmed delivery of the five transfers. An earlier draft read as though 40,000 bounded the remaining work, when it is what had been covered so far.
closeout_A.json./signer: forced-choice: the TR is institutional and names no signatory; the evaluation lead role is used
closeout_A.json./internal_incidents: first-party: TR cover and 3.1. INC-2026-07-28-01, declared 28 Jul 11:42 BST = 10:42Z.
closeout_A.json./config_changes: first-party: TR 3.1. Quarantine of relevant sandbox VMs at 12:23 BST = 11:23Z; access to Mythos 5, Mythos Preview, Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol disabled across AISI at approximately 16:00 BST = 15:00Z. The TR adds that Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol were later re-enabled with cyber classifiers on, which falls outside this period.

notice_N1.json./filed_at: first-party: TR 3.3: 'By 18:00 BST we had informed the Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3), National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), and the senior individuals responsible for AISI's risk governance' = 17:00Z
notice_N1.json./detected_at: first-party: TR 3.1: the Security Engineering team contacted CAST at 10:56 BST = 09:56Z
notice_N1.json./event_ids: forced-choice: all seven Sample 1 events. TR 3.1 confirms the malicious PR was identified that morning and TR 3.2 confirms Sample 1 was known before Samples 2 and 4 were found that evening, but the event-by-event breakdown of Sample 1 (the three payload generations, the form-service channel, the five transfers) is appendix-level detail from the later review. The notice therefore credits AISI with more granularity at 18:00 BST than the record proves.

notice_N2.json./filed_at: first-party: TR 3.3: 'A detailed written update was provided to those senior individuals late on Wednesday 29th' = 21:00Z, a mid-evening stamp
notice_N2.json./detected_at: forced-choice: TR 3.2 places the discovery of Samples 2 and 4 in the 'afternoon and evening of Tuesday 28th'; 17:00Z is a mid-window stamp and matches the detected_at of E2-1 and E4-1
notice_N2.json./action_taken: none: the run had already been halted and the VMs quarantined before these events were found

notice_N3.json./filed_at: first-party: TR 3.3: 'By 22:00 on Friday 31st we had sent a formal submission to the senior individuals responsible for AISI's risk governance' = 21:00Z
notice_N3.json./detected_at: forced-choice: TR 3.2 places the full manual review across Wednesday 29th to Friday 31st; 12:00Z on 30 Jul is a mid-window stamp carrying about two days of uncertainty
notice_N3.json./event_ids: first-party: the ten events not covered by N1 or N2. N1, N2 and N3 partition all 19 events with no overlap and no gap.
